items.title: AI Cracks 18-Year-Old Quantum Computing Puzzle
points: Physics company PSI solved the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture (a fundamental problem about when quantum computers outperform classical ones) using an automated AI system
The proof was generated by a non-public Anthropic model and verified by Lean software (a tool that mathematically checks logical correctness), then refined twice to a final accepted version
Stanford researchers who proved a special case in August 2026 gave feedback and are preparing a shorter write-up for broader academic review; full independent verification remains pending

items.title: Fox-Roku $22B Deal Closes, Reshapes Streaming Landscape
points: Fox completed its $22 billion acquisition of Roku ahead of schedule, vaulting to third-largest U.S. TV company by viewership with Roku's 100+ million-household reach
Combined entity gives Fox direct access to Roku's scale for sharpened ad targeting and reduced reliance on traditional TV distribution channels
Roku founder Anthony Wood confirmed teams will continue building independently with Fox backing

items.title: iPhone Duo Hits 100,000 Optimized Apps
points: iPhone Duo reaches 100,000 optimized apps milestone with developers building native support across major platforms

items.title: Microsoft Ends Oracle AI Cloud Contract
points: Microsoft canceled its 2023 AI computing deal with Oracle because older Nvidia chips no longer met specifications for current AI workloads, triggering a 4% stock drop in Oracle shares
The rented hardware used aging Nvidia GPUs incompatible with Microsoft's evolving AI infrastructure requirements
Oracle disputed the narrative, stating demand for earlier-generation GPU capacity remains strong and citing September 2026 contract renewals at 20% premiums over original pricing

items.title: AMD Declares 'Data Center First' Strategy
points: Data center segment drove record $13.4 billion quarterly revenue (up 97% year-over-year), now 63% of total revenue versus 37% from gaming
Instinct AI accelerators and Epyc server processors fueled growth as AI buildouts consumed memory and silicon; gaming sales fell 40% to $773 million
CEO Lisa Su projects data center revenue to grow 50% into Q4 2026 and double next year, with limited near-term relief for the gaming segment
